title: Russia says it downed a record 1,336 Ukrainian drones as Crimean bridge is hit
dek: Moscow's mayor said about 600 drones headed for the capital overnight. Ukraine says it struck an oil depot and a refinery in southern Russia, while the EU added 113 new names to its Russia sanctions list.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Russia said its air defences shot down 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight into Monday, the largest number it has reported for a single night, as drones struck the road and rail bridge that links Russia to occupied Crimea and forced it to restrict traffic for several hours. Moscow's mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, said about 600 drones had flown towards the Moscow region, and flights were restricted at several of the capital's airports, according to reports.

Ukraine's General Staff said its forces had hit an oil depot in Russia's Rostov region and the Ilsky oil refinery in Krasnodar region overnight. The strikes came the day European Union foreign ministers added 12 people and 101 entities to the EU's Russia sanctions list, and days before US President Donald Trump is due to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China.

## What happened

In a Telegram post at 8.10 am Moscow time (10.40 am IST), Mr Sobyanin said that between 5 pm on Sunday and 8 am on Monday "around 600" drones had flown towards the Moscow region, that most had been destroyed "at distant approaches" by the defence ministry's air defences, and that 191 had been neutralised as they approached the city itself. Russian aviation authorities temporarily restricted flights at airports including Vnukovo and Sheremetyevo, reports said. Russia's defence ministry put the night's total at 1,336 drones over several regions; its previous highest reported figure, for the night of 29 October, was 1,254, according to reports. Neither figure can be independently verified.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, wrote on Telegram that "the enemy struck the Crimean bridge" and that traffic would be restricted until roughly the middle of the day, with an operations headquarters set up in Kerch. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later described the damage as minor and said vehicles were still using the crossing, reports said. Russia's transport ministry said road traffic had been suspended temporarily for repairs while rail services continued; several passenger trains to Crimea were delayed, according to reports. Ukraine had not publicly commented on the bridge strike by Monday evening.

Ukraine's General Staff said on Telegram that the "main target" of the past day was the Flash Energy oil depot in Azov, in Rostov region, near Rostov-on-Don, which it called the main logistics hub of Russia's southern group of forces; it said explosions were followed by a fire. In a second post it said Ukrainian forces had hit the Ilsky refinery in Krasnodar region, damaging the AT-4, AT-5 and AT-6 crude distillation units, where processing of crude oil begins, and a petrol production complex. It listed refineries in Saratov, Kirishi, Omsk, Volgograd and Nizhnekamsk as earlier targets this month. Russian regional authorities said six people were injured in Krasnodar region and three in Azov, and one person was killed and another injured in Belgorod region, according to reports.

Ukraine's air force said Russia had launched 158 attack drones at Ukraine overnight, of which 131 were shot down or jammed by 8 am. Ukraine's deputy energy minister, Artem Nekrasov, said strikes had caused power cuts in six regions (Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Odesa, Ternopil and Cherkasy) and that Russia had carried out 116 deliberate attacks on energy and oil and gas sites in the past week, reports said. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had launched more than 2,300 drones, 1,590 guided bombs and 15 missiles at Ukraine during the week.

## The EU's new listings

Meeting in Brussels on Monday, EU foreign ministers imposed asset freezes on 12 individuals and 101 entities, and travel bans on the individuals, citing Russia's attacks on Ukraine's civilian infrastructure, according to reports of the Council's announcement. Nearly 50 of the entities are Russian banks and financial institutions. Also listed are the sole shareholder of the online retailer Wildberries, the majority owner of the e-commerce company Ozon, companies that manage Russian refineries and the St Petersburg oil terminal, and companies from the United Arab Emirates, China, the Seychelles and Oman that buy Russian crude oil products, reports said. The reported summary did not name any Indian company.

France's foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, said France and the United Kingdom would host an international conference in Paris on 4 December on Russia's "shadow fleet", the tankers that carry Russian oil around Western restrictions, reports said. Last Friday, EU naval forces boarded a tanker in the Mediterranean that the bloc's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, said had been sailing under a false flag.

## Background

The 19 km Kerch bridge carries a road and a railway across the Kerch Strait between Russia's Krasnodar region and Crimea, which Russia seized and annexed in 2014; most countries do not recognise the annexation. It has been a supply route for Russian forces since the full-scale invasion in February 2022 and has been attacked before, including by a truck bomb in October 2022 and by naval drones in July 2023.

Ukraine has made Russia's oil refineries a main target this autumn. Mr Zelensky said on Sunday that the strikes had disabled more than 55% of Russia's refining capacity, a claim that Russian officials have not confirmed and that could not be verified.

Peace efforts have stalled. Talks between US, Russian and Ukrainian officials in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November produced an agreement on a prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on a ceasefire, according to reports. Russia says it will not stop fighting unless Ukraine withdraws from four regions Moscow claims and drops its bid to join NATO. Sweden's foreign minister, Maria Malmer Stenergard, called Russia's demands "absurd" on Monday, reports said. Mr Zelensky said last week that US negotiators had floated NATO membership for Ukraine in return for leaving the Donbas region.

## Why it matters for India

India is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude oil, and its refiners and importers have to keep track of each new round of Western sanctions on Russian oil companies, buyers and tankers. Strikes on Russian refineries tend to cut Russia's exports of diesel and petrol and can push up global fuel prices Brent crude was trading at about $95 a barrel on Monday. Any deal on Ukraine reached among the US, Russia and China in Shenzhen would also shape India's balancing of its ties with Washington and Moscow.

## What happens next

Trump, Putin and Xi are expected to meet at the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen later this week, though US officials have said Ukraine will not be the focus, according to reports. Ukraine's allies are due to meet this week in the Ramstein group, which co-ordinates weapons supplies, and the separate "coalition of the willing", where Kyiv is seeking defence funding for 2027, according to reports. EU governments will discuss the 22nd sanctions package later this week.

## Key numbers

- 1,336: Ukrainian drones Russia says it shot down overnight, its highest reported figure
- About 600: drones Moscow's mayor said flew towards the capital region; 191 stopped near the city
- 158: Russian drones launched at Ukraine overnight, by Ukraine's count; 131 downed or jammed
- 113: new EU sanctions listings (12 people, 101 entities)
